## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)
*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and SuttaCentral data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*
The *Akkharukkhapetavatthu* (Pv 48), translated as "The Axle", is a Buddhist narrative in the *Petavatthu* collection of the Pali Canon [SuttaCentral]. The core theme outlined for the text addresses the question of what result arises from the giving of a small gift [SuttaCentral].
In secondary scholarship, the work is cited in passing by Bimala Churn Law, who refers readers to the story of the *Akkharukkhapeta*—alongside other narratives such as the *Kumarapeta*, *Pañcaputtakhādakapeta*, and *Goṇapeta*—in his study *The Buddhist Conception of Spirits* while discussing beings reborn as spirits (*petas*) on account of unwholesome deeds [Law 1926]. SuttaCentral records four translations of the text across four languages [SuttaCentral].
Neither SuttaCentral nor DharmaNexus identifies any established parallels or significant text reuse for this sutta: SuttaCentral records no curated parallels, and automated analysis by DharmaNexus reveals no Pali-internal reuse passages nor cross-language matches in Chinese, Sanskrit, or Tibetan corpora [SuttaCentral; DharmaNexus].
